consumer:dependent.us_half@i1040gi:p21.question_phrase: live with you in the United States (the 50 states and the District of Columbia) for more than half of 2025; time a child presumed kidnapped was missing because of the kidnapping does not
consumer:dependent.us_half@i1040gi:p21.source_phrase: Kidnapped child, "the credit for other dependents, and the earned income credit (EIC). For details, see Pub. 501 (Pub. 596 for the EIC)."
consumer:dependent.us_half@i1040gi:p21.reason: The gate dependent.kidnap_eic reads the EIC residency answer on actual time, which the question states by excluding the time missing; a No is the case in which the p. 21 kidnapped-child treatment would be needed, and the gate refuses it.

consumer:dependent.born_died@p501:p9.question_phrase: born in 2025, or did this person die in 2025? A child born in 2025 is born alive only if state or local law treats the child as born alive ... Do not list a stillborn child.
consumer:dependent.born_died@p501:p9.source_phrase: Death or birth, "Your qualifying child or qualifying relative who lived with you for more than half the part of the year they were alive"
consumer:dependent.born_died@p501:p9.reason: The head of household death-or-birth rule applies to a qualifying child or relative, which can only be a child born alive (p501 p. 13); the added live-birth and stillborn sentences restate that and do not change who was born or died in 2025.

consumer:dependent.born_died@p503:p3.question_phrase: born in 2025, or did this person die in 2025? A child born in 2025 is born alive only if state or local law treats the child as born alive ... Do not list a stillborn child.
consumer:dependent.born_died@p503:p3.source_phrase: Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person, "a person who was born or died in 2025"
consumer:dependent.born_died@p503:p3.reason: A qualifying person for the dependent care credit must be a dependent or a person who could be one, which a stillborn child cannot be (p501 p. 13); the birth-or-death question means the same thing on this page.

consumer:dependent.self_support@i1040gi:.question_phrase: provide over half of their own support for 2025

consumer:dependent.self_support@i1040gi:.reason: dependent.qc_tiebreak reads the Step 1 support test to decide whether the person is your own qualifying child; p. 19 is cited for the meaning of taxpayer, not of support, and the Step 1 meaning is unchanged.

consumer:dependent.other_claimant@i1040g.question_phrase: meet the conditions to be the qualifying child of any other person for 2025, under the dependent rules or under the EIC rules
consumer:dependent.other_claimant@i1040g.source_phrase: Who wasn’t a qualifying child (see Step 1) of any taxpayer for 2025. For this purpose, a person isn’t a taxpayer if ...
consumer:dependent.other_claimant@i1040g.reason: The gate combines this answer with dependent.other_nontaxpayer to reach p. 19's 'qualifying child of any taxpayer'; the question is broader (it includes the EIC rules), so a broader Yes can only keep the refusal, never compute a qualifying relative the page excludes.

consumer:dependent.other_claimant@p501:p.question_phrase: meet the conditions to be the qualifying child of any other person for 2025
consumer:dependent.other_claimant@p501:p.source_phrase: Sometimes, a child meets the relationship, age, residency, support, and joint return tests to be a qualifying child of more than one person.
consumer:dependent.other_claimant@p501:p.reason: The tie-breaker applies to a child who is the qualifying child of another person and of you; the question asks the first half and the gate tests the second from your own Step 1 answers.

consumer:dependent.joint_return@i1040gi:.question_phrase: Is a joint return being filed for 2025 that includes this person ... other than one filed only to claim a refund
consumer:dependent.joint_return@i1040gi:.source_phrase: Who wasn’t a qualifying child (see Step 1) of any taxpayer for 2025
consumer:dependent.joint_return@i1040gi:.reason: The gate reads the Step 1 joint return test to decide whether the person is your own qualifying child; p. 19 is cited for the meaning of taxpayer, and the Step 1 meaning is unchanged.

consumer:dependent.joint_return@p501:p15.question_phrase: Is a joint return being filed for 2025 that includes this person ... other than one filed only to claim a refund
consumer:dependent.joint_return@p501:p15.source_phrase: meets the relationship, age, residency, support, and joint return tests to be a qualifying child of more than one person
consumer:dependent.joint_return@p501:p15.reason: The joint return test named on p. 15 is the Step 1 test the question asks.

consumer:dependent.other_nontaxpayer@p50.question_phrase: is every such other person not a taxpayer for 2025? A person is not a taxpayer if they are not required to file ...
consumer:dependent.other_nontaxpayer@p50.source_phrase: Sometimes, a child meets the relationship, age, residency, support, and joint return tests to be a qualifying child of more than one person.
consumer:dependent.other_nontaxpayer@p50.reason: The gate does not let this answer lift the tie-breaker refusal: when the person passes your own qualifying child tests the gate refuses whatever this answer is, and the answer matters only for a person who is not your qualifying child (the p. 19 test).

consumer:dependent.joint_return@i1040gi:.question_phrase: Is a joint return being filed for 2025 that includes this person ... other than one filed only to claim a refund
consumer:dependent.joint_return@i1040gi:.source_phrase: Even if a child meets the conditions to be the qualifying child of more than one person, only one person can claim the child
consumer:dependent.joint_return@i1040gi:.reason: dependent.eic_tiebreak reads the EIC joint return condition (p. 41, Step 3) to decide whether the child is your EIC qualifying child; the meaning is the one dependent.eic_child already reads.

consumer:dependent.other_claimant@i1040g.question_phrase: meet the conditions to be the qualifying child of any other person for 2025, under the dependent rules or under the EIC rules (which have no support test)
consumer:dependent.other_claimant@i1040g.source_phrase: Even if a child meets the conditions to be the qualifying child of more than one person, only one person can claim the child
consumer:dependent.other_claimant@i1040g.reason: The EIC tie-breaker applies to a child who is the qualifying child of another person under the EIC rules and is yours; the question includes the EIC rules and the gate tests the rest from your EIC answers.

consumer:dependent.disabled@i1040gi:p19.question_phrase: permanently and totally disabled at any time in 2025, that is, unable to engage in any substantial gainful activity
consumer:dependent.disabled@i1040gi:p19.source_phrase: If the person was permanently and totally disabled, see Exception to gross income test (p. 19), the term defined on p. 21
consumer:dependent.disabled@i1040gi:p19.reason: Step 4's gross-income exception uses the term the question now defines from p. 21.

consumer:dependent.relationship@i1040gi:.question_phrase: child (son, daughter, stepchild, eligible foster child ...); household_member (any other person ... who lived with you all year as a member of your household)

consumer:dependent.relationship@i1040gi:.reason: Head of household Test 2 sorts persons by the same relationship categories, distinguishing the all-year household member the question names.

consumer:dependent.divorced_rule@i1040gi.reason: Step 1's residency test points to the exceptions on p. 21, of which the rule for children of divorced or separated parents is the one this question names; the line refuses on yes, and p. 17 sets no other definition of the rule.

consumer:dependent.married@i1040gi:p17.question_phrase: Was this person married at the end of 2025 ... or is a joint return being filed for 2025 that includes this person

consumer:dependent.married@i1040gi:p17.reason: The question asks for every person on a joint return (and every married person), so every person Step 1's joint-return condition reaches is refused through it; the line's own joint-return test reads dependent.joint_return.

consumer:dependent.married@i1040gi:p19.question_phrase: Was this person married at the end of 2025 (a person legally separated under a decree of divorce or separate maintenance is not married)
consumer:dependent.married@i1040gi:p19.source_phrase: 3. Was your qualifying relative married? Yes. See Married person
consumer:dependent.married@i1040gi:p19.reason: Step 4, question 3 asks the same married test the question asks, and the line refuses on yes rather than applying Married person.

consumer:dependent.married@i1040gi:p41.question_phrase: Was this person married at the end of 2025 ... or is a joint return being filed for 2025 that includes this person
consumer:dependent.married@i1040gi:p41.source_phrase: If the child was married, see Married child, later; Who isn't filing a joint return for 2025 or is filing a joint return for 2025 only to claim a refund
consumer:dependent.married@i1040gi:p41.reason: The EIC step sends a married child to Married child (married at the end of 2025), which the question asks; the line refuses on yes, and its own joint-return test reads dependent.joint_return.

consumer:dependent.married@i1040gi:p14.question_phrase: Was this person married at the end of 2025 (a person legally separated under a decree of divorce or separate maintenance is not married), or is a joint return being filed for 2025 that includes this person (including one filed by this person with a spouse who died during 2025
consumer:dependent.married@i1040gi:p14.source_phrase: 2. Your unmarried qualifying child who isn't your dependent
consumer:dependent.married@i1040gi:p14.reason: Head of household Test 2 item 2 needs the child to be unmarried; the question's no is unmarried at the end of 2025 with legal separation counted as unmarried and a spouse who died in 2025 counted as married, the year-end status the filing-status rules use.

consumer:dependent.joint_return@i1040gi:.question_phrase: Is a joint return being filed for 2025 that includes this person ... other than one filed only to claim a refund of withheld or estimated tax
consumer:dependent.joint_return@i1040gi:.source_phrase: Who isn't filing a joint return for 2025 or is filing a joint return for 2025 only to claim a refund of withheld income tax or estimated tax paid
consumer:dependent.joint_return@i1040gi:.reason: The EIC qualifying-child test words the joint-return condition and its refund-only exception exactly as Step 1 does, which the question asks.

consumer:dependent.tin@i1040gi:p22.question_phrase: an SSN, ITIN or ATIN issued on or before the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions), or have you applied for an ITIN or ATIN for this person by then
consumer:dependent.tin@i1040gi:p22.source_phrase: You must enter each dependent's social security number (SSN) ... If your dependent won't have a number by the date your return is due, see What if You Can't File on Time?

consumer:dependent.tin@i8863:p2.question_phrase: an SSN, ITIN or ATIN issued on or before the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions), or have you applied for an ITIN or ATIN for this person by then
consumer:dependent.tin@i8863:p2.source_phrase: Students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)
consumer:dependent.tin@i8863:p2.reason: Read with Pub. 970 ("If an ATIN or ITIN is applied for on or before the due date ... and the IRS issues an ATIN or ITIN as a result of the application, the IRS will consider the ATIN or ITIN as issued on or before the due date"), an application by the due date meets the issued-by-the-due-date test, as the question counts it.

consumer:dependent.edu_1098t@i8863:p2.reason: Page 2 sets no Form 1098-T condition of its own; the line reads the p. 1 requirement, the question's own definition, for the dependent it treats as an eligible student here.

consumer:eic.died_2025@i1040gi:p41.question_phrase: Did your spouse die in 2025, or are you preparing this return for someone who died in 2025?
consumer:eic.died_2025@i1040gi:p41.source_phrase: Were you, or your spouse if filing a joint return, at least age 25 but under age 65 at the end of 2025? ... If your [spouse died in 2025 or if you are preparing a return for someone who died in 2025, see Pub. 596]
consumer:eic.died_2025@i1040gi:p41.reason: The age question on p. 41 continues onto p. 42 with the death condition the question asks in the same words; the line refuses on yes.

consumer:f1040.status@i1040gi:p15.source_phrase: You can check the "Qualifying surviving spouse" box in the Filing Status section ... if all of the following apply

consumer:f8960.unsupported@i8960:p13.question_phrase: a section 1411 net operating loss ... a deductible investment expense other than investment interest or state and local tax; or another net investment income adjustment

consumer:f8960.unsupported@i8960:p18.question_phrase: a deductible investment expense other than investment interest or state and local tax; or another net investment income adjustment

consumer:f8960.unsupported@i8960:p22.question_phrase: a CFC or PFIC holding; a section 911 exclusion
consumer:f8960.unsupported@i8960:p22.source_phrase: If you didn't exclude any amounts from your gross income under section 911 and you don't own an interest in a CFC or PFIC, your MAGI is your AGI
consumer:f8960.unsupported@i8960:p22.reason: The two conditions that make MAGI differ from AGI are the ones the question asks; the line copies AGI and refuses on yes.

consumer:f8962.alloc@f8962:p1.question_phrase: Did any Marketplace policy ... cover someone in your tax family and also someone who is not in it ... or were you divorced or legally separated during 2025 while enrolled in a policy with your former spouse
consumer:f8962.alloc@f8962:p1.source_phrase: Are you allocating policy amounts with another taxpayer or do you want to use the alternative calculation for year of marriage? See instructions

consumer:f8962.other@f8962:p1.question_phrase: someone enrolled was not lawfully present ... a qualified small employer HRA ... or an individual coverage HRA ... any part of a month's premium was not paid by the due date ... advance payments were made for someone who is in no one's tax family

consumer:f8962.other@f8962:p1.reason: Line 24 sets no condition of its own; the conditions that bar or change the credit are the i8962 rules the question quotes, and the line refuses on yes.

consumer:person.edu_1098t@i8863:p3.question_phrase: Did the student receive a 2025 Form 1098-T from the educational institution? Answer yes also if the institution was not required to furnish one

consumer:person.itin_applied@i1040gi:p17.question_phrase: have you applied for an ITIN, or for the renewal of your expired ITIN, on or before the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions)
consumer:person.itin_applied@i1040gi:p17.source_phrase: If you want to claim the credit for other dependents, you, and your spouse if filing jointly, must have either an SSN or ITIN issued on or before the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions)
consumer:person.itin_applied@i1040gi:p17.reason: p. 22 deems an ITIN applied for by the due date and issued as a result to be issued by the due date for the credit for other dependents (amb.2025.ctc_spouse_itin_application keeps the deeming off the child tax credit's id_count).

consumer:person.x_other@f5329:p2.question_phrase: excess HSA contributions from an earlier year when you have no Form 8889 for 2025
